full_description:
Summary

We are looking for native Indonesian speakers or experienced document sourcing specialists to help us collect authentic, publicly available documents written in Indonesian for an AI training project.

The project focuses on sourcing real-world documents with meaningful content, natural language usage, and varied layouts. The collected data will help improve AI systems' multilingual document understanding and processing capabilities.

Native-language knowledge is strongly preferred to ensure documents are authentic, correctly written, and clearly identifiable as Indonesian.

Document Requirements

All submitted documents must meet the following criteria:

Documents must be written in the target language (Indonesian).

Each document must contain at least 300 words.

Documents must have a natural, meaningful, and readable structure.

Each document must contain at least 2 structural elements, such as:

Tables

Key-value fields

Signatures

Figures or images

Clickable fields

Text sections or headings

Lists, columns, or form fields

Documents must be authentic and publicly available online.

A valid source URL must be provided for every submitted document.

The actual document must be downloadable in PDF, JPG, PNG, or another suitable file format.

Webpage screenshots, screen captures, browser snapshots, or text snippets are not acceptable as final submissions.

Documents must be clearly identifiable as being written in Indonesian.

Documents must be complete, legible, and of reasonable quality.

Avoid duplicate documents, irrelevant content, or files with incomplete pages.

Preferred Document Types

We are looking for documents across a wide range of domains, including but not limited to:

Loans and mortgage documents

Newspapers and news articles

Legal documents and official notices

Contracts and agreements

Financial reports

Environmental reports

Tax documents

Handwritten doctor's notes

Handwritten applications

Receipts and invoices

Certificates of analysis

Insurance documents

Hospital claims and patient forms

Checks and deposit slips

Educational documents and academic reports

Government forms and public administration records

Business letters and correspondence

Manuals, guides, and informational brochures

Domain-Based Sourcing

We will provide a list of specific domain names/websites from which documents must be sourced.

Freelancers must search within the assigned domains and identify documents that meet all project requirements.

Documents must be sourced only from the provided domains unless additional sources are explicitly approved.

Freelancers are responsible for verifying the language, word count, structure, authenticity, downloadability, and quality of each document before submission.

The original downloadable file and its corresponding source URL must be provided for every submission.

Important Guidelines

The focus is on sourcing real documents, not creating or translating documents.

Documents must come from legitimate public sources or accessible document repositories within the assigned domains.

Each submission must include the original source URL for verification.

Do not submit artificially generated, recreated, or manually assembled documents.

Do not combine content from multiple documents to meet the word-count requirement.

For multi-page documents, one self-contained page may be selected, provided it independently meets all requirements.

Ensure the document is readable, properly formatted, and clearly in the target language before submitting.

Do not source private, confidential, or sensitive personal information.

Duplicate documents or previously submitted files will not be accepted.

Payment

$2 per approved document

Payment is provided for documents that pass quality review and meet all project requirements.

Rejected or non-compliant submissions will not be eligible for payment.

Accuracy, authenticity, language quality, and compliance with the sourcing guidelines are essential for approval.

Project Duration

This is an ongoing project with recurring batches of work. Freelancers who deliver consistent, high-quality submissions may be invited to participate in future batches.

Android App Testers Wanted – Ring by Daysli

We are looking for reliable Android users to test 'Ring by Daysli', a new lightweight communication application designed to make everyday conversations simpler, faster and more convenient.

Our web application, [login to view URL], is already operational and tested. We are now focusing on testing our native Android application on real smartphones before its wider public release.

Project responsibilities

Each selected freelancer will be required to:

- Install the Ring Android application through our Google Play testing programme.
- Create a dedicated testing account following our registration instructions.
- Actively use and test the application.
- Recruit five additional genuine Android testers.
- Help those five testers register and install the application.
- Encourage each of those five testers to bring another five Android testers.
- Coordinate testing activities and collect feedback from their testing community.

Each freelancer should aim to establish a testing group of 31 participants, including themselves.

All participants must be genuine Android users who voluntarily agree to participate and actively test the application.

Testing requirements

We want testers to evaluate the following:

- Application installation and registration.
- Google sign-in and account setup.
- Incoming and outgoing voice calls.
- Sending and receiving messages.
- Finding contacts by username.
- Incoming call and message notifications.
- Receiving calls when the application is closed or the phone is locked.
- Our “Ring when we're both free” feature.
- Missed, declined and cancelled calls.
- Communication between Android and web users.
- Application speed and responsiveness.
- Battery and mobile data consumption.
- Performance on Wi-Fi and mobile networks.
- Network interruptions and reconnection.
- Overall design, usability and reliability.

Testing accounts

All participants must register dedicated testing accounts using the instructions we provide.

Selected freelancers will receive:

- Google Play testing access instructions.
- Test account registration instructions.
- Tester invitation instructions.
- Testing guidelines.
- Bug reporting and feedback submission instructions.

Participants must follow these instructions so that testing activity can be distinguished from genuine customer activity.

Feedback and deliverables

Each freelancer must submit a consolidated report containing:

- Number of registered and active testers.
- Android phone models and operating system versions tested.
- Features successfully tested.
- Bugs and technical problems discovered.
- Screenshots or screen recordings of issues.
- Genuine feedback from participating testers.
- Suggestions for improving the application.
- Comparison with existing communication applications such as WhatsApp, Viber, Telegram and Signal.
- Whether testers would consider using Ring for everyday communication.

Applicant requirements

- Own an Android smartphone.
- Have access to a Google Play account.
- Be able to recruit and coordinate additional Android testers.
- Have good communication skills.
- Be willing to actively test the application and provide constructive feedback.
- Be available for continued testing during the agreed testing period.

Previous application testing experience is welcome but not mandatory.

We welcome applicants from all countries and are particularly interested in testing across different Android versions, smartphone brands, network providers and geographical locations.

When applying, please include

- Your country.
- Your Android smartphone brand and model.
- Your Android version.
- Your ability to recruit and coordinate additional Android testers.
- Your availability.
- Your previous testing experience, if any.
- Your proposed total project fee.

Payment will be based on genuine testing, coordination and completed feedback deliverables, not registrations alone.

Successful freelancers may be considered for ongoing paid testing opportunities for future Ring releases.

Summary 

We are looking for native Aragonese speakers or experienced document sourcing specialists to help us collect authentic, publicly available documents written in Aragonese for an AI training project. 

The project focuses on sourcing real-world documents with meaningful content, natural language usage, and varied layouts. The collected data will help improve AI systems' multilingual document understanding and processing capabilities. 

Native-language knowledge is strongly preferred to ensure documents are authentic, correctly written, and clearly identifiable as Aragonese.

All submitted documents must meet the following criteria: 

Documents must be written in the target language (Aragonese). 

Each document must contain at least 300 words. 

Documents must have a natural, meaningful, and readable structure. 

Each document must contain at least 2 structural elements, such as: 

Tables 

Key-value fields 

Signatures 

Figures or images 

Clickable fields 

Text sections or headings 

Lists, columns, or form fields 

Documents must be authentic and publicly available online. 

A valid source URL must be provided for every submitted document. 

The actual document must be downloadable in PDF, JPG, PNG, or another suitable file format. 

Webpage screenshots, screen captures, browser snapshots, or text snippets are not acceptable as final submissions. 

Documents must be clearly identifiable as being written in Aragonese. 

Documents must be complete, legible, and of reasonable quality. 

Avoid duplicate documents, irrelevant content, or files with incomplete pages. 

Preferred Document Types 

We are looking for documents across a wide range of domains, including but not limited to: 

Loans and mortgage documents 

Newspapers and news articles 

Legal documents and official notices 

Contracts and agreements 

Financial reports 

Environmental reports 

Tax documents 

Handwritten doctor's notes 

Handwritten applications 

Receipts and invoices 

Certificates of analysis 

Insurance documents 

Hospital claims and patient forms 

Checks and deposit slips 

Educational documents and academic reports 

Government forms and public administration records 

Business letters and correspondence 

Manuals, guides, and informational brochures 

Domain-Based Sourcing 

We will provide a list of specific domain names/websites from which documents must be sourced. 

Freelancers must search within the assigned domains and identify documents that meet all project requirements. 

Documents must be sourced only from the provided domains unless additional sources are explicitly approved.

The original downloadable file and its corresponding source URL must be provided for every submission. 

Important Guidelines 

The focus is on sourcing real documents, not creating or translating documents. 

Documents must come from legitimate public sources or accessible document repositories within the assigned domains. 

Each submission must include the original source URL for verification. 

Do not submit artificially generated, recreated, or manually assembled documents.

Payment

Payment is provided for documents that pass quality review and meet all project requirements. 

Rejected or non-compliant submissions will not be eligible for payment. 

Accuracy, authenticity, language quality, and compliance with the sourcing guidelines are essential for approval. 

Project Duration 

This is an ongoing project with recurring batches of work. Freelancers who deliver consistent, high-quality submissions may be invited to participate in future batches.
